title: Lightening-Transformer: A Dynamically-Operated Optically-Interconnected Photonic Transformer Accelerator
problem: Photonic accelerators efficiently support weight-static operations in CNNs but struggle with the dynamic and full-range tensor multiplication inherent in attention-based Transformers. Existing photonic tensor core designs cannot efficiently handle Transformer workloads despite photonics' energy efficiency and speed advantages.
motivation: Transformers (Vision Transformers and LLMs) are computationally expensive and widely deployed, so demonstrating efficient photonic acceleration for Transformers could unlock significant energy and performance benefits for advanced machine-learning workloads.
method: The accelerator uses light-based computing cores connected in a grid, where each core performs vector multiplication through optical interference. Multiple cores connect via optical links that efficiently broadcast data between them. Unlike earlier photonic accelerators that only handled fixed values, this design dynamically adjusts to handle the full range of varying inputs that Transformers need.
key_novelty: The first Transformer accelerator using photonic cores that can dynamically handle the varying calculations and full input ranges that Transformers require, instead of just fixed-value operations.
contributions: Lightening-Transformer: first photonic accelerator efficiently supporting Transformer architectures
DPTC (Dynamically-Operated Photonic Tensor Core): novel photonic tensor core enabling dynamic matrix multiplication
Photonic interconnects for efficient inter-core broadcast and system integration
>2.6x energy efficiency and >12x latency improvements over prior photonic accelerators

metrics.speedup: >12x latency reduction vs prior photonic accelerators
metrics.energy: >2.6x energy reduction vs prior photonic accelerators; lowest energy vs electronic accelerators
metrics.energy_delay_product: 2-3 orders of magnitude lower than electronic Transformer accelerators
